history.period: Original 16th century (per Wikipedia; a British report dates a brick structure to mid-18th c.); rebuilt 1921
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the most prominent and well-documented shrine called 'Lakshmi Narayan Temple' in Amritsar is the Shri Durgiana Temple, also known as the Lakshmi Narayan Temple, Durga Tirath and Sitla Mandir (verify if the CSV intends a different, smaller standalone shrine of this name). The Durgiana Temple, near the Lohgarh/Hathi Gate, is the second most visited holy site in Amritsar after the Golden Temple. It is famous for its architectural similarity to the Shri Harmandir Sahib: the main temple stands in the middle of a sacred lake (sarovar), reached by a marble bridge, with gold-plated domes. The original temple dates to the 16th century and is recorded in the Amritsar District Gazetteer of 1893 ('Devi dwara' around Durgiana Sarovar). It was rebuilt in 1921 by Guru Harsai Mal Kapoor in the style of the Golden Temple; the foundation stone of the present structure is credited to Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya (1924 per some sources). Legend links the site to the Ashvamedha Yajna of Lord Rama: it is believed Luv and Kush tied the ritual horse here, and a tree in the courtyard is said to be where they captured Hanuman. The complex includes the Bara Hanuman Mandir, the Shitla Mata temple, Sat Narain and Radha Krishna shrines, and a Tulsidas temple with a handwritten Ramayana. A Langar Bhawan serves daily meals.

name: Shri Lakshmi Narayan Mandir
town_description: Amritsar is Punjab's spiritual capital, founded by Guru Ram Das in the 16th century around the Golden Temple (Shri Harmandir Sahib). The city is a major Sikh and Hindu pilgrimage centre; the Durgiana/Lakshmi Narayan Temple stands near the old city's Lohgarh/Hathi Gate, close to the railway station and Jallianwala Bagh.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport (Amritsar), about 11 km from the city; taxis and autos to the temple.
travel.railway: Amritsar Junction (1.5 km; verify) on the Delhi-Amritsar line; the temple is close to the station and Hathi Gate.
travel.road: Well connected by NH-3/GT Road to Jalandhar (80 km), Ludhiana (135 km) and Delhi (450 km); local autos and cycle rickshaws reach the temple in the old city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Navratri (Dussehra) for the Langooranwala Mela, though very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typically open daily from early morning to late evening (verify exact hours locally). Note: sale of tobacco, liquor and meat is restricted within a 200 m radius of the temple.
